interface.signature: def checkMirrorTree(n: int, e: int, A: list[int], B: list[int]) -> int:

preconditions.expression: n >= 1 and e >= 1 and len(A) == 2 * e and len(B) == 2 * e
preconditions.description: n and e are positive integers, and A and B each contain exactly 2*e elements representing edges.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in zip(A[::2], A[1::2])) and all(1 <= u <= n and 1 <= v <= n for u, v in zip(B[::2], B[1::2]))
preconditions.description: All nodes in edges of A and B are within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: return_value == 1 if (lambda: (lambda build_adj(edges): {u: [] for u in range(1, n + 1)} if not edges else {u: [v for v in edges if v[0] == u] for u in range(1, n + 1)}) and (lambda adj_A, adj_B: (lambda is_mirror(root_A, root_B, adj_A, adj_B): root_A == root_B and all(is_mirror(adj_A[root_A][i], adj_B[root_B][-i - 1], adj_A, adj_B) for i in range(len(adj_A[root_A]))))))(build_adj(zip(A[::2], A[1::2])), build_adj(zip(B[::2], B[1::2]))) else 0)() else 0
postconditions.description: Returns 1 if the two trees are mirror images of each other, otherwise returns 0. The trees are mirror images if their adjacency lists satisfy the mirror property recursively: for every node, its children in tree A must mirror the children of the corresponding node in tree B in reverse order.
